name: Bread-thickened sauce
summary: A sauce that a cook binds with soaked and strained bread. The sauce gets body and a soft texture, and it carries spice and acid.
how: Soak white bread in broth, vinegar or verjuice for a short time.
Grind the bread with spice in a mortar and strain the paste through a cloth.
Heat the sauce gently and serve it beside a roast or over boiled meat.

origin.note: Le Viandier gives bread as the main binder of its sauces, as in the cameline sauce.

adoptions.via: Italian and French banquet kitchens kept bread as a binder beside the first butter sauces.
